name: Example: Computing the Variance of a Data Set Using the Formula
problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
4, \: 5, \: 4, \: 7, \: 8, \: 11, \: 3
$$
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
\sigma^2 = \overline{x^2} - (\overline{x})^2,
$$

where $\overline{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overline{x^2}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (4+5+4+7+8+11+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 42 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot ({4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (16+25+16+49+64+121+9) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 300 \\  & =\frac{300}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{300}{7}-{(6)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{300}{7}-36 \\  & =\frac{300-252}{7} \\  & =\frac{48}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
